answer_text:
Looking at this problem, I need to find the minimum number of 1×1 square frames (each covering the 4 edges of one unit cell) to cover every edge of an 18×15 grid.

## Setting Up the Problem

The 18×15 grid has 270 unit cells. Each frame covers exactly the 4 edges of one cell. I need every edge in the grid to be covered by at least one frame.

**Key observation:** Boundary edges can only be covered by the single adjacent cell, while internal edges can be covered by either of the two adjacent cells.

## Counting Mandatory Boundary Frames

Every cell on the boundary **must** be selected (since boundary edges have only one adjacent cell):

- Top row: 18 cells
- Bottom row: 18 cells  
- Left column (excluding corners): 13 cells
- Right column (excluding corners): 13 cells

**Total boundary cells: 18 + 18 + 13 + 13 = 62**

## Solving the Internal Cell Problem

The internal cells form a **13 × 16 grid** (rows 2–14, columns 2–17), containing 208 cells.

Edges between a boundary cell and an internal cell are already covered by the boundary frame. So I only need to ensure every edge **between two internal cells** is covered by at least one of them.

This is exactly the **Minimum Vertex Cover** problem on a 13×16 grid graph!

## Applying König's Theorem

Since the grid graph is bipartite, by König's theorem:
$$\text{Min Vertex Cover} = \text{Max Matching}$$

Since 16 is even, the checkerboard coloring gives exactly 104 black and 104 white cells. In each row of 16 cells, I can pair them as (1,2), (3,4), (5,6), ..., (15,16) — giving 8 edges per row × 13 rows = **104 edges** forming a **perfect matching**.

Therefore:
$$\text{Min Vertex Cover} = \frac{13 \times 16}{2} = 104$$

## Final Calculation

$$\text{Minimum frames} = \underbrace{62}_{\text{boundary cells}} + \underbrace{104}_{\text{internal cells}} = 166$$

\boxed{166}
